summary: The Goshen Township Board of Trustees held a regular meeting featuring a police accreditation presentation by the Ohio Collaborative Law Enforcement Accreditation Program, recognizing the Goshen Township Police Department for achieving state accreditation. The board also adopted a zoning resolution for minimum street frontage requirements, approved holding trick-or-treat at Fire Station 18, accepted the resignation of Officer Lara, and entered executive session to discuss employee compensation and appointments.
decisions: Motion to adopt the agenda passed
Motion to approve payment of bills (September 9–22, 2026) passed
Motion to adopt Resolution R042-2026 establishing minimum street frontage requirements, permitting flag/panhandle lots in R2 and R3 districts, and prohibiting easement-only or landlocked lots passed
Motion to hold trick-or-treat at Fire Station 18 on October 31, 2026 passed
Motion to accept resignation of Officer Lara effective October 21, 2026 passed
Motion to enter executive session at 6:22 PM under ORC 121.22(G)(4) and ORC 121.22(G)(1) passed
Motion to adjourn at 7:43 PM passed
action_items: Fire Chief to coordinate trick-or-treat event at Station 18 on October 31, 2026
Fire department to equip and place new ladder truck in service within the next couple months
Police department to process Officer Lara's resignation and benefit time through October 21, 2026
Zoning Director Langenheim to implement new street frontage and flag lot zoning standards following Resolution R042-2026
key_amounts: 25 foot minimum road frontage required for flag lots
500 foot maximum depth for flag lots before requiring a variance
notable_topics: Ohio Collaborative Law Enforcement Accreditation awarded to Goshen Township Police Department
New ladder truck delivered — first in approximately 15-20 years
Zoning resolution R042-2026 for minimum street frontage, flag lots, and landlocked lot prohibition
Trick-or-treat event returning to Fire Station 18
Resignation of Officer Lara (citizen of Luxembourg, accepted airline job)
Executive session regarding employee compensation, appointment, and bargaining
Clermont County Engineers annual meeting attended by administrator and service director
Commendation email for Officer Perkins regarding deer crash response
attendees: Ed Burthammer (Director of Law Enforcement Services, Office of Criminal Justice Services)
Charity Daddy Wingo (Program Manager, Ohio Collaborative)
notes: Trustee Allen was absent due to a family emergency; thoughts and prayers were expressed. The executive session lasted approximately 80 minutes (6:22 PM to 7:42 PM). The new ladder truck was described as a significant long-term investment expected to serve for at least 15 years. Officer Lara holds dual citizenship in the U.S. and Luxembourg and speaks multiple languages. The mobile home previously on fire department property has been removed.
title: BOT 9-22-26
